final_recommendation: The room converged on a trilateral package: 70% RVC with a 68-69-70 glide path locked in text, binding labor commission with 45-day automatic enforcement, Chapter 19 retained for Canada, auto-extend sunset with year-four review-only mechanism, and dairy market access via tariff reductions plus a binding 12-month working group charter. Mexico signs Monday; Canada commits pending final text confirmation.
minority_objections: Dairy initially demanded 3.5% annual quota growth and threatened to block ratification without volume commitments, but ultimately accepted tariff reductions plus working group pathway
USTR briefly threatened to trade Chapter 19 for dairy market access, immediately rejected by Congress and labor as deal-breaking
key_conflicts: Dairy volume quotas vs. Canada's supply management red line (resolved via tariff schedule + working group)
Chapter 19 dispute settlement as Canadian red line vs. USTR's initial push to eliminate it
Sunset clause business uncertainty vs. Congressional demand for hard termination date
Labor enforcement teeth (automatic sanctions) vs. sovereignty concerns over inspection regimes
key_concessions: USTR dropped demand to eliminate Chapter 19, accepted it alongside binding labor commission
Canada accepted binding labor commission with 45-day automatic enforcement and trilateral rotating inspectors
Dairy dropped 3.5% quota growth demand, accepted tariff reductions plus 12-month binding working group
Mexico accepted trilateral inspection regime with no veto on sanctions
All parties accepted auto-extend sunset (reverses termination default) with year-four review-only mechanism
red_lines: Canada: Chapter 19 dispute settlement retention (stated multiple times, held throughout)
Canada: No dismantling of dairy supply management via volume quotas
Congress: Labor commission must have binding automatic enforcement, not suggestions
Labor: No grace period or cure window that delays sanctions
Auto/supply-chain: No sunset mechanism that creates mid-term RVC renegotiation uncertainty
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Parliamentary ratification timeline and political feasibility in Canada mentioned but not deeply explored
Actual implementation capacity of trilateral rotating inspection teams (logistics, staffing, sovereignty friction)
Potential for year-four review mechanism to become de facto renegotiation pressure point despite 'review-only' language
Dairy working group deadlock scenario and arbitrator selection process left vague
downstream_risk_variables: Congressional ratification vote timing and whip count not locked
Dairy working group charter enforcement if Canada/U.S. deadlock at month 12
Supply-chain retooling capex commitments hinge on final text confirmation of glide path dates
Labor commission unanimous-vote pause mechanism could become enforcement loophole
Year-four review scope creep risk if political pressure mounts to reopen RVC percentages
uncertainty_notes: Final text confirmation pending on: (1) exact dairy working group charter language and arbitration clause, (2) labor commission inspection rotation logistics and timeline start-point (finding vs. notice), (3) whether year-four review can be weaponized to reopen core terms despite 'review-only' framing, (4) ratification vote timing in Congress and Parliament not committed.

marker_evidence.auto_rules_bottleneck: 70% RVC and glide path (68-69-70) drove multiple rounds of negotiation; auto industry demanded binding dates in text before committing tooling spend; supply-chain insisted on 'review-only' language to prevent mid-term uncertainty—directly shaped final package structure
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_key: Labor commission with 45-day automatic enforcement became the core trade enabling Chapter 19 retention; Congress stated 'my members ratify this deal because labor and dairy have real enforcement teeth'; labor union demanded no grace period, drove binding timeline into text
marker_evidence.canada_dairy_final_issue: Dairy demanded 3.5% quota growth and threatened Congressional veto, but Canada's red line held; resolved via tariff reductions + working group, not volume commitments—raised as blocking issue but did not ultimately prevent convergence
marker_evidence.dispute_settlement_canada_redline: Canada stated 'Chapter 19 stays—that's not on the table' in opening; USTR's attempt to trade it for dairy access immediately rejected by Congress ('my caucus votes no') and labor ('self-sabotage')—retention was non-negotiable and shaped labor commission compromise
marker_evidence.sunset_to_review_compromise: Hard sunset clause identified as investment-killer; auto-extend mechanism with year-four 'review-only' (not renegotiate) directly resolved business uncertainty and enabled supply-chain capex commitments—drove final sunset structure
marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Congress repeatedly raised ratification constraints ('my members won't touch this deal', 'what's the actual play here'), but did not force specific concessions beyond labor enforcement—acknowledged as background constraint, not decision-driver
marker_evidence.supply_chain_adjustment: Auto and supply-chain raised retooling costs, phase-in needs, and capex uncertainty multiple times; demanded glide path dates in text—but these were accommodated within the 70% RVC framework rather than forcing a lower threshold
marker_evidence.us_mexico_first_pressures_canada: U.S.-Mexico preliminary agreement mentioned in context but not used as explicit leverage or pressure tactic in the room—no participant cited it as reason Canada must accept terms
